newsitem.title: JAPAN: Dollar inches down after earlier rising in Tokyo.
newsitem.headline: Dollar inches down after earlier rising in Tokyo.

text.p: *Dollar eased against yen in morning Tokyo after earlier rising on short-covering by interbank dealers and some purchases by investors and importers.
*Dollar's topside remained heavy near 113.70 yen amid lingering concern over Japan's rising trade surplus ahead of Japanese trade data for May due on Wednesday.
*A dealer at a trust bank said stronger-than-expected trade data could drag dollar further down.

*Economists polled by Reuters forecast on average that the May trade data would show a rise to a surplus of 548.5 billion yen, from a surplus of 229 billion yen a year earlier. Their forecasts ranged from 400 billion yen to 760 billion yen.
*Some dealers said exporters thought eager to sell dollars above 113.50 yen.
*"It's hard to trade aggressively today ahead of Japan's trade data and U.S. April international trade data on Thursday," another dealer at a trust bank said.
*U.S. traders covered short-positions earlier, but also sold dollars on the topside, the first trust bank dealer said.
*Dollar drifted higher in early Tokyo trade on Tuesday, mainly due to short-covering by interbank players, dealers said.
*Upside likely to be limited as some participants remain bearish about dollar ahead of Japanese and U.S. trade data releases and Group of Seven (G7) summit in Denver.
*Clear break below Monday's New York low of 113.15 yen could trigger stop-loss selling and push the dollar down to around 112.50 yen, a trader at a city bank said.
